correctness.rationale: Conditional on T nonfocal draws, their multiset has the same law as a length-T prefix of an independent renormalized iid list or a uniform permutation of the nonfocal census individuals. Thus unconditional richness can be realized as R_T + 1_{T<n} and singleton-conditioned richness as 1+R_{n-1}. For T<n use monotonicity; for T=n use R_n − R_{n-1}≤1. The census prefix exists whenever the target event has positive probability; T=n is used only if feasible. The indicator covariance equals event probability times the conditional mean gap, and summing over species includes zero-probability events with contribution zero. In the iid case n≥2, singleton conditioning guarantees K≥2 while the all-focal outcome has positive probability; the strict increment of a strictly increasing g at 2 ensures strict covariance. For every 2≤r≤n, the supplied uniform iid example and census example have positive exact-r events with K≤n−r+1, whereas all n distinct nonfocal species occur with positive unconditional probability. The argument includes n=1 and full-census equality cases. The proof was reconstructed directly; the bundled code and certificate were inspected, not executed. The reported 28 counterfamily checks are elementary assertions, not full distribution enumerations.

value.rationale: Richness and singleton frequency are standard sampling summaries. This gives a distribution-level guarantee, not just a moment sign, that survives arbitrary abundance heterogeneity and the switch from iid draws to a census. The sharp failure of every higher fixed multiplicity identifies why singleton conditioning is special and makes the result useful without claiming general association.
